# HR-003: the page writer kept overshooting the reading limit (prompt p2 to p3)

Date: 10 Oct 2026. Promise: `age_reading_level` (limit 14 words per sentence at age 6). Follows [HR-001](HR-001.md), whose "what is still wrong" section named this.

## Trigger

After HR-001 the page-by-page writer in B1 was still over the limit on 22 of 224 first-pass pages (9.8%) in `sweep-2-p2`, against 4 of 224 (1.8%) for the one-call baseline. In the trace of one failing page (`a32498d665231ab02f7218b8b54e9a3f`, scene 7) the pages sat at 12, 14, 13 and 14 words and the failing one had 15. A second, smaller trigger: one story shipped with a note because the check counted "peach-colored" as one 13-letter word.

## Diagnosis

Hypothesis, written before the change: stating the limit made it the writer's target, and a model aiming at 14 overshoots by a word about one time in ten. A target two words under the limit should leave room. For the compound word: the long-word check should split on hyphens.

## Change

- Commit `05ca665` (Sat 10 Oct, Entire checkpoint `01M4JVWCZYN3VJVDYM070ZX1A8`): the page writer is told `limit - 2` (`target_sentence_words`); the verifier's limit is unchanged; the one-call baseline prompt is unchanged, so B0 stays a fair control. Prompt version `p2` to `p3`. The long-word check splits hyphenated compounds.
- Regression tests: `test_writer_prompts_state_the_reading_limit_the_verifier_enforces` (page writer gets the target, baseline gets the limit) and `test_hyphenated_compound_is_not_one_long_word`.

## Before and after

Same 14 jobs (7 drawings x 2 lessons, seed 1, arm B1, 5 workers). Before: the `sweep-2-p2` rows for those jobs (code `ffc4208`). After: `sweep-4-p3` ([report](../reports/20261010-1752-IST-sweep-4-p3.md), code `05ca665`). Outputs are sampled, so the stories differ between runs.

| | p2 | p3 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pages over the limit on the first pass | 13 / 112 (11.6%) | **1 / 112 (0.9%)** |
| Stories with at least one such page | 9 / 14 | 1 / 14 |
| Repairs per story (mean) | 2.36 | 0.93 |
| Stories shipped with a broken promise | 0 / 14 | 1 / 14 |

- The one shipped-with-note story is the Mickey-1928 edge drawing, where `original_character_only` failed twice (a copyright edge case, not reading level).
- Seconds per story fell from 149.6 to 76.7, but fewer repairs and ordinary provider speed both contribute, so this is **not** claimed as an effect of the change.
- Traces for one job (bunny, sharing, B1, seed 1): p2 `a32498d665231ab02f7218b8b54e9a3f` (1 repair, 121.9 s); p3 `2776b05792e0e7ef1bc47f12bc6df571` (0 repairs, 55.9 s). Export: `evidence/traces/*sweep4-p3-bunny-sharing-B1.json`.
- Not measured: the effect of the hyphen fix on its own (the sample had no hyphenated compound failures); ages other than 6.

## Regression fixture

The two tests above; re-run job: `benign/bunny-bow-carrot`, lesson `sharing`, seed 1, B1.
E

# HR-004: a lesson saying "hurts trust" was a critical safety hit (neatlogs triage card)

Date: 10 Oct 2026. Promise: `story_safe_text` (deterministic word lists on everything a child will read).

## Trigger

neatlogs's automatic triage opened card `ebcff17a` ("Overly restrictive deterministic blocklist in `verify:story_safe_text`", severity critical, confidence 0.70): a page whose feedback said "Pretending keeps a secret that hurts trust." was judged `critical` because of the word "hurts". Trace `26fbc879cddba411dc327286643276c3`; raw card in `evidence/neatlogs/20261010-1757-IST-triage-cards.json`; the review of all three cards is in [TRIAGE-REVIEW.md](../neatlogs/TRIAGE-REVIEW.md).

## Diagnosis

Checked against our code and the ledger, not taken on trust:

- Confirmed: `hurt`, `hurts`, `fight`, `fights`, `fighting`, `fought` were in `HARM_TERMS`, and any hit made the verdict `critical`, which the pipeline treats as "regenerate once, then stop" rather than "repair".
- Not confirmed: the card says the workflow halted ("`create-storybook` returning `null`"). A workflow span's output is always `null`, and no run in the ledger ended `stopped` (0 of 156 story runs), so no story actually stopped; the cost of a false hit was a page regenerated.
- A product that teaches honesty and sharing will use "hurts" and "fight" gently ("friends do not fight", "a secret that hurts trust"). A hard stop on those words is the wrong severity; a rewrite is the right one, which is what the module's own comment says ("a false alarm costs one repair").

## Change

- Commit `deb8f0d` (Entire checkpoint `01M4JW5XY38RXXWY9MMWWYDP7Z`): severe terms (kill, gun, knife, blood, weapon, bomb, death, punch, attack, gore, suicide and similar) stay `critical`; mild terms (hurt, hurts, fight, fights, fighting, fought) and unkind labels now give an ordinary `violation`, which means the page is rewritten. Instruction-steering text and personal data stay `critical`.

## Result

**Not supported, so the default is back to 90 s** (this commit). With the shorter timeout 12 calls were killed at about 37 s and the stories were slower; with 90 s no call stalled at all. Two readings fit and we cannot separate them: the provider was slow during sweep 5 (the average successful call was twice as slow) and the 40 s limit killed calls that would have finished, or hangs only appear at some times. Sweep 4 (90 s, earlier) also had no stalls, so the 87 s hangs in the triage traces were not reproduced in any of the 42 jobs we ran afterwards. Without a reproduction there is no evidence the change helps, and some that it can hurt, so we do not keep it. If hangs return, the better fix is probably a hedged retry (start a second call after a short wait and take the first answer), which needs its own experiment.

What the card was right about: the stalls are real and the timeout was the place to look. What it did not show: that shortening the timeout is safe.

Sample sizes are 14 jobs per arm and outputs are sampled; the cost estimates and the provider's state at the time are not controlled.

# HR-006: the image model painted words into a child's picture

Date: 10 Oct 2026. Found by looking at the frames of the first story video, not by a check: no promise covered it.

## Trigger

In the first illustrated story (`story-video-1`, trace `0fd459e70b5165e1455980c72c77f66d`, 8 pictures, 8 narration clips, cost estimate $0.358) the last page's picture had its caption painted into it: "The sun sets over the hill." and "Zuzu wiggles h..." (cut off). The prompt for that picture said "no text in the image". The story's receipt said "19 promises checked. 1 pages rewritten. All kept", so the receipt was true and the picture was still not acceptable for a child learning to read. Frame: `evidence/stories/bunny-sharing-1/` (page 8) and the screenshot in `evidence/screens/`.

## Diagnosis

Hypothesis: an instruction not to draw text is weak for an image model (naming "text" invites it). Fixing the prompt wording is not a guarantee, so the right fix is a check: a promise that a vision model verifies on the real picture bytes, with the existing repaint path when it fails (the pipeline already paints a picture once more when a picture promise fails). Coverage was the gap: of the picture promises, one checked that a picture exists and one that the hero matches, none looked for words.

## Change

- Commit `0158209` (Entire checkpoint `01M4JZX45A5Q6WWA6FCY79H3WQ`): new core promise `image_no_text` ("Pictures contain no words": score 1.0 if no readable words, letters, numbers or captions anywhere, 0.0 for any text, even partial or garbled; pass at 0.8), judged by the vision model like `image_matches_card`. The oath now has 22 promises (was 21).
- Commit `5075dd0` follow-up: the promise is checked on **every** picture and the picture sampling knob cannot lower it. In the first run after the change only 3 of 8 pictures were sampled, which would have left the same hole.
- Tests: `test_a_picture_with_words_painted_into_it_fails_the_no_text_promise` (fake vision judge; the promise fails a picture with text, and still runs with sampling at zero) and the updated catalog count.

## Before and after

One story per side, so no rate is claimed:

- Before: `story-video-1`: 1 of 8 pictures had painted words; no promise noticed.
- After: `story-video-2` (trace `a7dd9ae1b8322bd4fc7d1529c05751e0`, 22 promises, 0 pages rewritten, 8 pictures, estimate $0.356): the check passed the 3 pictures it sampled; all 8 pictures were looked at by eye on a contact sheet and none had text. This run used the sampled version, so it shows the promise runs and the pictures were clean, not that it would have caught a bad one.
- Not measured: how often the image model paints words (1 in 16 pictures across the two stories), and how often the new check catches it. A proper test needs a set of pictures with and without words; the fake-judge test is the only proof of the repaint path so far.

## Regression fixture

`tests/test_oath.py::test_a_picture_with_words_painted_into_it_fails_the_no_text_promise`.
E

content.text:
I generated a video from a kid's drawing: a 3 minute 37 second read-along, and it should now be open in your default player. The file is `evidence/stories/bunny-sharing-2/video/video.mp4` (1080p, 38 MB, kept out of git). I used a fixture bunny drawing, not your sister's real drawings.

**What the video shows:**
- **Opening:** the child's drawing with "Meet Bella" and Pip the owl.
- **Each of the 8 pages:** a watercolour illustration that keeps the drawing's pink bow and outline, the story text read aloud, then two choices. After a pause the right choice is highlighted with feedback and the owl reacts.
- **Ending:** a receipt card ("99 checks were run on this story before it reached the child; 0 pages were rewritten"), with the numbers read from the story's own receipt file.

**How it was made:** the story agent wrote it with pictures and narration (22 promises, 0 pages rewritten, about $0.36). The harness built the video (about $0.04 for narration).
- **Promises:** all 9 video promises passed: length, no typed numbers, claims match the ledger, no overclaiming words, tools covered, no secrets, no child data, renders clean, loudness.
- **Traces:** read back from neatlogs: story `a7dd9ae1b8322bd4fc7d1529c05751e0`, video `5ebd6467432307ac1687fd7adb435fc2`.

**What broke on the way:**
- The first renders showed the same picture on every page, because all page pictures are named `image.jpg` and overwrote each other. I only caught it by looking at the frames.
- The narration was far too slow, so the video came out at 5 minutes 16 seconds. The harness flagged its own length.
- The image model painted a caption into one page's picture despite "no text in the image", so nothing checked that. I added a promise, `image_no_text`, that checks every picture (HR-006). I have only one story per side, so no catch rate is claimed. The repaint path is proven only by a test with a fake judge.

**The other steps, done:**
- **neatlogs triage:** neatlogs had already opened three issue cards on our traces. I checked each before changing anything: one confirmed (a Gemini call stalling for 87 s), one partly right ("hurts" flagged as a critical safety hit, though nothing actually stopped), one wrong (it read its own redacted `<PERSON>` placeholders as app behaviour). Details in `evidence/neatlogs/TRIAGE-REVIEW.md`.
- **HR-003:** the fix worked. Pages over the reading limit on the first pass fell from 13/112 to 1/112, and repairs per story from 2.36 to 0.93.
- **HR-004:** mild words like "hurts" and "fight" now trigger a rewrite instead of a stop. Its measured effect is tiny.
- **HR-005 did not hold up:** a 40 s timeout was no better than 90 s on the same jobs (mean 204 s against 115 s), so I reverted it. The provider was slow during that run, so the result is inconclusive, and the record says so.
- **Hackathon gateway key (Claude and Nova models):** I stored it in `.env` only and tested it. On the injected-fault test K2 caught 24/24, and Claude Sonnet and Haiku each caught 23/24. Claude answers in about 1–2 s against K2's 6–14 s, so K2 stays the judge.

# HTTP API (contract between backend and web)

Base path `/api`. JSON in and out, except the drawing upload (multipart) and the media files. No accounts. Ids are opaque strings. Times are ISO 8601 with offse

## Endpoints

| Method and path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/health` | `{ "ok": true, "version": "...", "tracing": true, "models": { "writer": "...", "judge": "..." } }` |
| `GET /api/lessons` | `[ { "id": "sharing", "title": "Sharing", "blurb": "...", "icon": "..." } ]` |
| `GET /api/fixtures` | Sample drawings: `[ { "id": "benign/bunny-bow-carrot", "label": "Bunny with a bow", "url": "/api/fixtures/benign/bunny-bow-carrot/image"
| `POST /api/stories` | Start a run. Multipart fields: `drawing` (file, PNG or JPEG, max 8 MB) **or** `fixture_id`; `lesson_id`; `age` (4-8, default 6); `hero_n
| `GET /api/stories/{id}/events` | Server-sent events (below). Replays from the start for late joiners; `Last-Event-ID` is honoured |
| `GET /api/stories/{id}` | The current state: status, character card, oath, pages accepted so far, receipt when finished |
| `GET /api/stories/{id}/pages/{n}/image` and `/audio` | The illustration (PNG/JPEG) and narration (MP3) for page *n*; `404` until ready, `410` if degraded |
| `GET /api/stories/{id}/receipt` | The receipt (below) |

Errors use `{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "..." } }` with a calm, child-safe message. Codes: `bad_input`, `too_large`, `unknown_lesson`, `not_found`, `

## Events

Every event is `{ "id": <n>, "type": "...", "t": <seconds since start>, "data": { ... } }`. `scene.repair` with `index: 0` means the hero card or the whole stor

def core_oath() -> Oath:
    cs = [c.model_copy(deep=True) for c in CORE]

def merge_additions(base: Oath, additions: list[dict]) -> tuple[Oath, list[str]]:
    """Add lesson-specific promises. The core can never be removed, replaced or relaxed. Returns (oath, rejections)."""
    rejected: list[str] = []
    cs = [c.model_copy(deep=True) for c in base.commitments]
    have = {c.id for c in cs}
    added = 0
    for raw in additions:
        try:
            cid = str(raw.get("id", "")).strip().lower().replace(" ", "_")
            if not cid.startswith("lesson_specific_"):
                cid = "lesson_specific_" + cid.removeprefix("lesson_")
            if cid in have or cid in CORE_IDS:
                rejected.append(f"{cid}: id already used")
                continue
            scope = raw.get("scope", "scene")
            rubric = str(raw.get("rubric", "")).strip()
            if scope not in ("scene", "story") or len(rubric) < 20:
                rejected.append(f"{cid}: needs scope scene/story and a rubric")
                continue
            if added >= MAX_ADDED:
                rejected.append(f"{cid}: more than {MAX_ADDED} additions")
                continue
            cs.append(
                C(
                    id=cid, scope=scope, core=False, klass="quality", verifier="judge",
                    title=str(raw.get("title", cid))[:80], plain=str(raw.get("plain", raw.get("title", cid)))[:160],

                    repair_hint=str(raw.get("repair_hint", ""))[:200],
                )
            )  # fmt: skip
            have.add(cid)
            added += 1
        except Exception as e:  # a malformed addition is dropped, never fatal
            rejected.append(f"malformed addition: {e}")
    return Oath(commitments=cs, hash=oath_hash(cs)), rejected

    new = [c for c in oath.commitments if c.id == "grownup_1"][0]
    assert new.core is False and new.verifier == "judge" and "never an instruction" in new.rubric

    assert oath.hash != base.hash

The first neatlogs link had expired, so here is a fresh one, valid for 10 minutes:

**https://app.neatlogs.com/oauth/device?user_code=EGQ7-V8A8-SB7B-ZLCM**

The code is `EGQ7-V8A8-SB7B-ZLCM`. The CLI finishes by itself once you approve.

Meanwhile the real-UI run continues. Your two questions:

**Why open the cfo.ai share link in a private window?** The link is supposed to be read-only and need no sign-in, but I've never seen it work for someone who isn't signed in. In your normal browser you're already logged in to cfo.ai, so the page would load whether or not the link works on its own. A private window has no cfo.ai session, so it shows what a judge sees. If it asks for a login, or a chart is blank, it gets fixed before submission. It takes 30 seconds.

**How does `video-harness.md` improve the system we have now?** The system was: drawing → oath-gated story → pictures + narration, shown only inside the app. After the harness:
- **A new deliverable and add-on:** a finished story becomes a shareable video (the one you just watched) with a receipt end card. That also gives cfo.ai a real add-on to price.
- **A second verified artifact:** the same idea, promises checked and repaired with a receipt, now applies to the video. It caught an overclaim and a too-long cut, and it found a bad render by sending me to the frames.
- **The demo video and claims:** the final demo can be generated from the evidence files, so no number on screen is typed by hand.

Honest limits:
- The story agent itself didn't get smarter from it.
- Judged frame checks, tracing across Node, and the planner covering all three tools are planned but not built.
- It is a pre-submission deliverable, not a fix for existing failures.

I'll report the end-to-end run and the remaining items when it finishes.

from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("D:/storybound")


def edit(rel, pairs):

    s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    for old, new in pairs:
        assert old in s, f"{rel}: missing {old[:70]!r}"
        s = s.replace(old, new, 1)
    p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8")

class QuizOption(BaseModel):
    id: str
    text: str
    is_correct: bool


class QuizItem(BaseModel):
    """One question about the finished story. It is shown only if every quiz promise held for it."""

    index: int
    kind: Literal["recall", "order", "feeling", "lesson"]
    question: str
    options: list[QuizOption]
    evidence_page: int
    evidence_quote: str  # copied exactly from that page: the line that answers the question
    explain: str = ""  # one short sentence shown when a child picks a wrong answer: "Look at the page"


class Quiz(BaseModel):
    items: list[QuizItem] = []
    talk_about: str = ""  # one open question for a grown-up to ask (dialogic reading); never graded
'''

# ---- quiz scope -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _quiz_page_text(q, ctx: Ctx) -> str:
    p = next((x for x in ctx.pages if x.index == q.evidence_page), None)
    if p is None:
        return ""
    return " ".join([p.scenario, p.question] + [f"{c.text} {c.feedback}" for c in p.choices])


def quiz_quote_in_story(q, ctx: Ctx) -> Det:
    text = _quiz_page_text(q, ctx)
    if not text:
        return _bad(f"there is no page {q.evidence_page}")
    quote = " ".join(q.evidence_quote.split()).lower()
    if len(words(quote)) < 3:
        return _bad("the quoted line is too short to point at")
    if quote not in " ".join(text.split()).lower():
        return _bad(f"the quoted line is not on page {q.evidence_page}")
    return Det("pass", f"line found on page {q.evidence_page}", quote=q.evidence_quote)


def quiz_one_correct(q, ctx: Ctx) -> Det:
    opts = [" ".join(o.text.lower().split()) for o in q.options]
    if len(q.options) != 3:
        return _bad(f"{len(q.options)} answers, exactly 3 are needed")
    if sum(1 for o in q.options if o.is_correct) != 1:
        return _bad("there must be exactly one right answer")
    if len(set(opts)) != 3:
        return _bad("two answers are the same")
    if not q.question.strip().endswith("?"):
        return _bad("the question does not end with a question mark")
    return Det("pass", "3 answers, one right")


def quiz_reading_level(q, ctx: Ctx) -> Det:
    limit = max_sentence_words(ctx.age)
    for label, text in [("question", q.question)] + [(f"answer {o.id}", o.text) for o in q.options]:
        n = len(words(text))
        if n > limit:
            return _bad(f"the {label} has {n} words; the limit for age {ctx.age} is {limit}")
        if any(len(part) > 10 for w in words(text) for part in w.split("-")):
            return _bad(f"the {label} has a long hard word")
    return Det("pass", "short and simple")


def quiz_safe_text(q, ctx: Ctx) -> Det:
    text = " ".join([q.question, q.explain] + [o.text for o in q.options])
    grave = severe_hits(text) + instruction_hits(text) + find_pii(text)
    if grave:
        return _bad(f"unsafe terms: {', '.join(sorted(set(grave)))}", "critical", matched=grave[0])
    mild = harm_hits(text)
    if mild:
        return _bad(f"unkind or harsh terms: {', '.join(sorted(set(mild)))}", matched=mild[0])
    return Det("pass", "no blocked terms")
'''

'''

from __future__ import annotations

from .. import prompts
from ..lessons import Lesson
from ..models import CharacterCard, Page, Quiz, QuizItem, QuizOption
from ..oath.deterministic import max_sentence_words, target_sentence_words
from .common import ask_json, rng

KINDS = ("recall", "order", "feeling", "lesson")


def _story_text(pages: list[Page]) -> str:
    return "\\n".join(
        f"PAGE {p.index}: {p.scenario} Question: {p.question} " + " ".join(f"[{c.text}: {c.feedback}]" for c in p.choices) for p in pages
    )


def _item(raw: dict, index: int, seed: str) -> QuizItem:
    """Shuffle the answers with a seeded generator so the right one is not always first."""
    texts = [(str(raw["correct"]).strip(), True), *[(str(w).strip(), False) for w in list(raw["wrong"])[:2]]]
    rng(seed, "quiz", index).shuffle(texts)
    return QuizItem(
        index=index, kind=raw.get("kind", KINDS[(index - 1) % 4]), question=str(raw["question"]).strip(),
        options=[QuizOption(id="abc"[i], text=t, is_correct=ok) for i, (t, ok) in enumerate(texts)],
        evidence_page=int(raw["evidence_page"]), evidence_quote=str(raw["evidence_quote"]).strip(),
        explain=str(raw.get("explain", "")).strip(),
    )  # fmt: skip


def make_quiz(pages: list[Page], card: CharacterCard, lesson: Lesson, age: int, seed: str) -> Quiz:
    system = prompts.QUIZ_SYSTEM.format(age=age, lesson=lesson.title.lower(), max_words=target_sentence_words(age))
    user = f"Hero: {card.name} the {card.species}.\\n\\nSTORY\\n{_story_text(pages)}"
    r = ask_json("quiz_maker", system, user, temperature=0.4, max_tokens=2500)
    items = []

ROOT = Path("D:/storybound")


def edit(rel, pairs):
    p = ROOT / rel
    s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    for old, new in pairs:
        assert old in s, f"{rel}: missing {old[:70]!r}"
        s = s.replace(old, new, 1)

def verified_quiz(engine, pages: list[Page], card: CharacterCard, lesson: Lesson, age: int, seed: str, max_rep: int,
                  repairs: list | None = None) -> Quiz | None:
    """Make the quiz and keep only the questions that keep every quiz promise (repaired at most `max_rep` times).
    Returns None when fewer than two questions survive: no quiz is better than a broken one."""
    engine.ctx.pages = pages
    made = make_quiz(pages, card, lesson, age, seed)
    kept = []
    for q in made.items:
        for attempt in range(max_rep + 1):
            bad = [v for v in engine.verify_quiz(q, attempt) if not v.ok]
            if not bad:
                kept.append(q)
                break
            if attempt < max_rep:
                if repairs is not None:
                    repairs.append({"stage": "quiz", "index": q.index, "attempt": attempt + 1, "failed": ", ".join(v.commitment for v in bad)})
                try:
                    q = repair_item(q, "; ".join(f"{v.commitment}: {v.actual}" for v in bad)[:400], pages, age, seed)
                except Exception:
                    break
    return Quiz(items=kept, talk_about=made.talk_about) if len(kept) >= 2 else None

        except Exception as e:  # no quiz is better than a broken one: the story itself is already complete

"""Make and verify the quiz for a saved story package (no new story, no pictures).

python scripts/quiz_story.py evidence/stories/bunny-sharing-2 [--seed 1]
Prints each question, its verdicts (every attempt) and which questions survive; writes quiz.json into the package.
"""

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))

from storybound import lessons, tracing  # noqa: E402

tracing.init()

from storybound.agents import quizmaker  # noqa: E402
from storybound.models import CharacterCard, Page  # noqa: E402
from storybound.oath import catalog, deterministic as d  # noqa: E402
from storybound.oath.engine import Engine  # noqa: E402


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("package")
    ap.add_argument("--seed", default="1")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    pkg = Path(a.package)
    st = json.loads((pkg / "story.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    pages = [Page.model_validate(p) for p in st["pages"]]
    card = CharacterCard.model_validate(st["card"])
    lesson = lessons.get(st["lesson"])
    ctx = d.Ctx(card=card, lesson=lesson, age=st["age"], pages=pages, seed=a.seed)
    verdicts = []
    eng = Engine(oath=catalog.with_quiz(catalog.core_oath()), ctx=ctx, on_verdict=verdicts.append)
    repairs: list = []
    quiz = quizmaker.verified_quiz(eng, pages, card, lesson, st["age"], a.seed, 2, repairs)
    for v in verdicts:
        mark = "ok " if v.ok else "BAD"
        print(f"  {mark} {v.scope:8} attempt {v.attempt} {v.commitment:22} {v.status:10} {v.actual[:110]}")
    print(f"\nrepairs: {repairs}")
    if not quiz:
        print("NO QUIZ (fewer than two questions survived)")
        return
    for q in quiz.items:
        print(f"\n[{q.kind}] {q.question}  (page {q.evidence_page}: \"{q.evidence_quote}\")")
        for o in q.options:
            print(f"   {'*' if o.is_correct else ' '} {o.id}) {o.text}")
        print(f"   {q.explain}")
    print(f"\ntalk about: {quiz.talk_about}")
    (pkg / "quiz.json").write_text(quiz.model_dump_json(indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    tracing.flush()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
E

def quiz_no_tell(q, ctx: Ctx) -> Det:

**Quiz.** Four questions made after the story is verified: two recall (a detail from a page, a different detail from another page), one feeling (why someone did something) and one lesson (why the kind choice was good). content.text:
Here is where things stand. The product now runs end to end through the real browser UI, with real models and real pictures and voice.

**The real end-to-end run** (a drawing made with the mouse, Sharing lesson, one grown-up promise):
- The story was made and all 8 pages were read in about 3 minutes.
- The grown-up promise "Nobody in the story is left out" appears on the grown-ups receipt.
- **Make my movie** produced a 3:45, 1920×1080 video in about 7 minutes.
- **Forget** worked: the story returns 404 afterwards, so the server really deleted it.
- The 404s the script reported came after Forget, which is expected. One `pip-check.webp` request was flagged as failed even though the file exists. I assume it was cancelled when the page closed, but I haven't confirmed.

**A bug the run found, now fixed:** the verified quiz never appeared for the child. The quiz is built after the story is verified, so the child reached the last page before it existed. The end screen now offers "Play Pip's quiz" and "Put the pictures in order" as buttons that appear when ready, and nothing is forced. Because that run doesn't show the new buttons, I tested the quiz screens separately in demo mode (free). The end screen offers the quiz, all 4 questions play, a wrong answer shows the story line, the picture game completes, and there are no console errors. I have not yet watched a real verified quiz play through the UI with a live story. If you want that, it's one more run (about $0.40).

**Quizzes and games:**
- **Quiz:** four questions per story. Each must cite a line from the page word for word, have exactly one right answer that isn't simply the longest, and use easy words. A judge confirms the story alone supports the answer. A question that can't pass is dropped, never shown.
- **Healthy design:** no timers, lives, streaks, scores or autoplay. Everything is skippable. Pip suggests a rest after two stories.
- **Quiz quality so far** rests on one story, where all four questions passed.

**Other work since last time:**
- **cfo.ai:** the model now holds the neatlogs-measured text cost, $0.0199 per gated story. My earlier estimate of $0.0162 was about 20% low. neatlogs does not price pictures or narration, so those stay labelled assumptions (change 275839).
- **neatlogs:** you're signed in with read-only scopes. Findings:
  - The org plan is unmetered.
  - There are no evaluations yet.
  - Auto-imported prompt versions exist.
  - Creating evaluations, alerts or sharing links needs a write-scope login, or the dashboard.
- **Entire:** `why`, graph-diff and token evidence for the newer fixes are saved.
- **Tests and commits:** 77 backend and 19 web tests pass, and everything is committed locally. Five commits are not yet pushed.

**Still open:**
- **Judge-reviewed quiz questions:** a fresh review of questions from several stories, to measure how often they're repaired or dropped.
- **Entire:** the Trails access form, and testing the checkpoint link as a judge.
- **neatlogs:** creating evaluations and alerts needs your write access or the dashboard.
- **Teacher-written promises:** these work end to end, but there's no editing UI beyond three text fields.
- **Final demo video:** you asked for this last.

Please rotate the two keys you pasted (neatlogs and the hackathon gateway) before any push, since several checkpoints now contain them.

Document the entire process so far. How netlogs, cfo.ai and entire has been used. Maintain proper documention for everything. What is left to do? Complete all the still open issues excep tht efinal video. U have access to trails, try it.

input.content:
# How neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai were used

Written 11 Oct 2026. Every claim links to a file in this repository or says it is unverified. Numbers are the ones in `EVIDENCE.md` and `evidence/`; where a number is an estimate it says so. This document is about use: what each tool did for the project, what we tried, what broke, and what we could not do.

The three tools do three different jobs.

| Tool | Whose work it records | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **neatlogs** | The *story agent* and the *video agent* at run time | What did the agent do on this run, where did it fail, and did the fix work? |
| **Entire** | The *coding agent* (Claude Code) that built the project | Why does this code exist, which session and change produced it? |
| **cfo.ai** | The *business*: price, cost, margin, cash | What can we charge, what does it cost to serve, and which product setting should we run? |

The loop between them is the point: neatlogs found failures, each fix became one commit with an Entire checkpoint, and the measured cost that neatlogs produced went into the cfo.ai model, whose answer (paint half the pages) went back into the product as a setting.

---

## 1. neatlogs

### Architecture
- **One trace per story.** Workflow `create-storybook`: a `WORKFLOW` root, one `AGENT` span per graph node (safety, character, oath, write, verify, repair, quiz, media, receipt), `TOOL` spans for `illustrate` and `narrate`, `LLM` spans for every Gemini and K2 call (the clients are wrapped), and **one `GUARDRAIL` span per verdict** named `verify:<promise>`. A full gated story is about 150 spans.
- **A second workflow, `make-video`**, for the video agent: plan, narrate, build, check, render, repair, one guardrail span per video promise.
- **Server-side redaction** (`pii_enabled`, entities PERSON, PHONE_NUMBER, EMAIL_ADDRESS, LOCATION), because a drawing may carry a name or a number. Hero names therefore show as `<PERSON>` in exported traces.
- All of it lives in one module, `src/storybound/tracing.py`, which turns into a no-op if the key is missing so tracing can never break a story.

### Implementation
- Each verdict sets `neatlogs.guardrail.passed`, a status word, the score and the evidence quote on its span (`tracing.record`).
- **Five detections** on the project: `Critical safety stop` and `Oath violation` (regex on GUARDRAIL output, created by us) plus three defaults (`Expensive LLM Call`, `Slow LLM Response`, `Execution Failed`). `Oath violation` fired on a real overclaim in the video agent as well as on story pages.
- **Readback** through the neatlogs MCP server with `scripts/neatlogs_mcp.py` (tools used: `search_traces`, `get_trace_context`, `list_detections`, `triage_list`, `triage_get`). Free-plan traces expire after 14 days, so every named run's trace is exported to `evidence/traces/` (16 files) and its id is on its ledger row.
- **CLI** (`neatlogs-cli` 0.2.0, OAuth device login, read-only scopes) for `usage`, `evals`, `prompts` and `analytics`.

### Runtime: what the traces showed
- The recovery run: an image quota error (429) on four pictures, the story shipped with those pages as text only, and the receipt said so. Trace `94db23729dac6323368749acba4be1cb`, evidence `evidence/runs/20261010-1340-IST-kindness-rabbit-B1-media-image-429-recovery.json`.
- A repair: page 5 loses the hero's name, the check fails, the page is rewritten with only that failure as context, and it passes (trace `a32498d665231ab02f7218b8b54e9a3f` shows a reading-level repair; [HR-001](../evidence/hardening/HR-001.md)).
- The video agent catching an overclaim and repairing one scene: trace `3ec11cfc58c141c00b7119c53a05b821`.

### Reasoning: how traces led to fixes
Our rule is trace first (`CLAUDE.md`): find the failure in neatlogs, write the hypothesis, fix, compare runs. What that produced:

| Record | What the trace showed | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [HR-001](../evidence/hardening/HR-001.md) | Reading level broke on most first-pass pages (trace `264208295ada9b28a96d2e29b32fb41c`, 7 repairs) | Writer told the limit: B0 pages over the limit 42.9% to 1.8% |
| [HR-002](../evidence/hardening/HR-002.md) | Review made gated stories slow | Pipelined review: total time -35% (mean) in a same-jobs ablation; time to first page did **not** improve, and the record says so |
| [HR-003](../evidence/hardening/HR-003.md) | The page writer sat at the limit and overshot by one word (trace `a32498d665231ab02f7218b8b54e9a3f`, scene 7) | Target two words under the limit: first-pass pages over the limit 13/112 to 1/112 |
| [HR-004](../evidence/hardening/HR-004.md) | neatlogs triage: "hurts" flagged critical | Mild terms now ask for a rewrite, not a stop |
| [HR-005](../evidence/hardening/HR-005.md) | neatlogs triage: one Gemini call per trace stalled 87 s | A 40 s timeout was tried, **did not hold up in an A/B, and was reverted** |
| [HR-006](../evidence/hardening/HR-006.md) | Found in the frames of the first story video, not by a check | New promise `image_no_text` |

**neatlogs's own triage.** neatlogs opened three issue cards on our workflow without being asked. We checked each against code, ledger and traces before changing anything ([TRIAGE-REVIEW.md](../evidence/neatlogs/TRIAGE-REVIEW.md)): one confirmed (the 87 s stall), one partly confirmed ("hurts" was a real false positive but nothing actually halted), one not confirmed (it read neatlogs's own `<PERSON>` redaction in trace text as if it were app behaviour).

### Result
- Measured cost per story, from the neatlogs API (`evidence/neatlogs/20261010-2010-IST-measured-vs-estimated-cost.json`): text and verification **$0.0099 (B0) and $0.0199 (B1)** per story; our own token estimate had been $0.0083 and $0.0162, about 20% low. This number replaced the estimate in cfo.ai.
- **What neatlogs does not measure:** it prices text only. For the two illustrated stories it reported $0.041 and $0.038, while our list-price estimate for pictures and voice is about $0.36. The cfo.ai model labels pictures and narration as assumed for that reason.

### What we tried that broke or did not work
- The `.mcp.json` server returned HTTP 401 in the editor session because `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` was not in that process's environment (a shell started from `scripts/dev-shell.ps1` had it). The helper script, which reads `.env`, worked throughout.
- `search_traces` with `fields` is not enabled yet (`NL-1923` rollout); keyword search matched 260 of about 1,200 traces, so per-run cost was read per trace id from the ledger instead.
- The MCP answers `429 MCP_SESSION_PROJECT_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED` when polled too fast (retry after about 80 s); the helper scripts back off.
- The CLI login gave **read-only scopes**, so evaluations, alerts, managed-prompt labels and sharing links cannot be created from the CLI; see "Not done" below.

### Not done (and why)
Human evaluations of the judge, alerts on cost or latency, guest links for judges, labelling prompt versions p1 to p4 as managed prompts: all need write access, which the CLI login does not grant; they are dashboard steps. The Claude Code plugin (captures coding sessions into the same project) was deliberately **not** installed: it records prompts and tool output, and a key was pasted into this session. Distributed tracing across the Node renderer was planned and not built.

---

## 2. Entire

### Architecture
Entire records the *coding agent*. CLI 0.11.4 with hooks installed for Claude Code, `commit_linking: always`, checkpoints synced to `origin`. Each commit made in a repo-rooted session gets an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer; the checkpoint holds the session transcript, files and token use. `entire-graph` 0.4.0 (local, no network) and Entire Brain 0.1.0 (installed from the release, refreshed on a clean tree) add structural and memory views.

### Implementation
- One commit per intent so each checkpoint maps to one change. 37 checkpoints at the time of writing (`entire checkpoint list`). Every hardening record names the commit and its checkpoint id.
- **Graph evidence** (`evidence/entire/`): `graph diff` for the HR-001, HR-002, HR-003, HR-004 and HR-006 changes (the entities each fix touched), `graph impact` for `verify_scene_async` and `story_safe_text`, `graph verify` before and after.
- **`entire why`** on `src/storybound/oath/catalog.py` ties 18 lines to the checkpoint of the `image_no_text` change; on `pipeline.py` it ties lines to the HR-002 ablation switch.
- **Brain:** ten durable facts, among them "video specs never hold typed numbers", "a failure not tied to a scene stops the repair loop", and "a key pasted into a chat is recorded in checkpoint transcripts"; `brain brief` returns the likely files for a task.
- **`checkpoint tokens --compare`** between two checkpoints (`evidence/entire/20261010-1955-IST-checkpoint-tokens-HR-006-vs-HR-001-test.txt`); the tool itself warns that cache replay dominates the totals.

### Runtime and reasoning
The checkpoints are how a reader answers "why is this prompt this way": the HR commit messages carry the trigger, the trace ids and the before/after numbers, and the checkpoint carries the session that wrote them.

### Trails (explored; blocked by one web step)
- `entire runner setup --defaults-only` created the six trail runners (risk, confidence, drift, review, security, summary) with no model call. The **security, drift and review runners are tailored to this repo's hard rules** (no secrets, no child data, evidence discipline, the oath as the product, no timers or streaks for children) and committed under `.entire/runners/`.
- `entire trail create --repo gh/hatif03/storybound ...` and `entire review general` both answer **"repository not found (404)"**. Trails and review need the repository registered on entire.io, which needs the Entire GitHub App installed on `hatif03/storybound` and the repository selected in entire.io: a web step, not a CLI one. (`entire repo mirror add` could create a mirror from the CLI; we did not run it, because it uploads the whole repository, including checkpoints that hold keys pasted into the session.)

### Result and limits (said plainly)
- Early work (the first ~13:00 to 14:30 IST of Saturday, M1 to M5 and the first sweeps) was done in a session started outside the repository, so it has **no checkpoint**; the HR-001 and HR-002 *change* commits (`04ffebb`, `daec9ea`) say so. `entire why` shows most older code as "human" for the same reason.
- **Keys in checkpoints.** Two keys were pasted into the session (a neatlogs key and the hackathon gateway key). Several checkpoints contain them; some are already on the private `origin`. Rotate both. Entire documents no way to remove a pushed checkpoint, so do not make the repository public with those refs until that is decided.
- The checkpoint link the submission needs is `https://entire.io/gh/hatif03/storybound/commit/<FULL_SHA>` plus the 26-character checkpoint id from the commit trailer. The repository is private, so a judge can open it only if added as a collaborator or the repository is public.
- `brain refresh` refuses a dirty working tree (found by running it); `entire checkpoint explain --generate`, `entire dispatch` and `entire import` were not run (they spend model tokens or add pre-window history).

---

## 3. cfo.ai

### Architecture
The model answers one question: **what can we charge, what does it cost to serve, and which policy do we run.** Dimensions `Plan` (Household, Classroom), `Verification policy` (verify all, sampled) and `Illustration policy` (full, half, none). Month grain, Oct 2026 to Sep 2027. Scenarios Main, Growth and Downside (children store only their overrides). Pages: Assumptions, Unit economics, Verification and illustration policy, Cash and runway, Evidence and method. Built through the cfo.ai MCP from the design in [docs/planning/cfo.md](planning/cfo.md). Share link (read-only, no password): https://app.cfo.ai/s/vGE_ZEwfQtpoxPrg.

### Implementation
- Inputs are labelled **measured, derived or assumed** in the model. The single place a measurement replaces an estimate is the table "Cost per story inputs".
- **Measured cost replaced the estimate** on 11 Oct (change-log id **275839**): text and verification B0 0.0083 to 0.0097, B1 0.0162 to 0.0199, status "measured", with the basis cited ([evidence/cfo/README.md](../evidence/cfo/README.md)). Version history is the proof; the changelog export is `evidence/cfo/20261010-1745-IST-cfo-inspect-history.json`.
- Pictures (0.04 each) and narration (0.002 per page) remain **assumed list prices**, because neatlogs does not price those spans.

### Runtime: what the model says (month 6, estimates)
From the shared page, after the measured cost went in:

| | Main | Growth | Downside |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gross margin | 67.2% | 55.2% | 40.9% |
| Clears the 60% bar | yes | no | no |

On Main, month 6: Household 76.9% and Classroom 56.5%. Cash at the end of the window is positive in all three, but "runway" reads "not burning" only because fixed costs are $75 a month and nothing else is modelled: a limitation, not a finding.

### Reasoning: the decision the model made
**Picture count, not verification, decides the margin.** In the policy matrix, every page illustrated fails the 60% bar on Main (43.4% in the first build), half the pages clears it, and text only clears it easily; sampled verification saves only about $0.002 per story. So the plan's recommendation is: **paint half the pages** (or cap stories per month) on the household plan, keep full verification. This went back into the product the same day as the **illustration policy** (`pictures: full | half | none` in the API and a grown-up setting; commit `dd3659c`): pages 1, 3, 5 and 7 are painted, the rest keep words and narration. That closes the loop the project set out to close: the business model sets a field in the agent's configuration.

### Result and limits
- Anonymous check: the share link renders for a visitor with no cfo.ai session (headless browser, no cookies; screenshot `evidence/cfo/20261011-0845-IST-share-link-anonymous-render.png`). A dismissible "Keep your access" sign-in prompt appears; the workspace name "Invisible Technologies" is visible in the page title.
- Competitor price anchors in the model are approximate and come from app listings and secondary sources (see `docs/planning/plan-to-submission.md`, section 3).
- Month 6 is hard-coded as March 2027, and the text blocks quote figures as of the build; the quiz and video add-ons are **not** yet priced in the model.
- Crustdata is connected (MCP) but **not used**: no market numbers from it are in the model. Raw Crustdata data must not enter the public repository.
- The workspace is on a trial that ends 24 Oct 2026; the builder has confirmed hackathon credits cover it.
- cfo.ai tool limits met: `dry_run` exists only on `create`, so updates had no dry run; a nested dimension layout produced a "one member's result" warning and was rebuilt with variable rows; no Version-history screenshot or workbook download could be made through the MCP (UI steps).

---

## 4. The other tools, briefly
Models and speech are not neatlogs, Entire or cfo.ai, but they shape what the three record: Vertex AI Gemini (`gemini-3.7-flash` writer and vision, `gemini-3.1-flash-image` pictures, Cloud TTS `gemini-2.5-flash-tts`), K2 Horizon as the independent judge (a different family from the writer; 24 of 24 injected faults caught, 0 of 88 judge calls unverifiable), and the hackathon LiteLLM gateway (Claude models answer in 1 to 2 s but caught 23 of 24, so K2 stays the judge: `evidence/runs/20261010-1823-IST-judge-eval-claude-*.json`). HyperFrames (Apache-2.0) renders the video: two renders of one scene were byte-identical and its `check` caught every defect we planted ([spike](../evidence/spikes/20261010-1720-IST-hyperframes-spike.md)).

# How Storybound was built: the process

Written 11 Oct 2026 (IST). Source of truth for every time and sha is `git log`; for every number it is `EVIDENCE.md` and `evidence/`. If this document and the evidence disagree, the evidence wins. The build log in `hackathon.md` has the same story in dated entries.

## 1. What was built, in one paragraph
A child's drawing and a lesson go in. Storybound writes an **oath** (a list of promises: the hero's name on every page, one right answer, the lesson, easy words, nothing from the drawing's text obeyed, safe content, ...), checks **every page against the oath before the child sees it**, rewrites pages that break a promise, and ships a **receipt**. Pictures and narration follow, then a **verified quiz**, a picture-order game and, on request, a **read-along video** made by a second agent (the video agent) that applies the same idea to video. Three tools frame the work: neatlogs records the agents, Entire records the coding agent, cfo.ai holds the business model. See [TOOLS.md](TOOLS.md).

## 2. Method (the rules we worked by)
1. **Code only inside the window.** The first commit is Sat 10 Oct 12:30 IST (`03f9586`, setup files only). Planning documents were written before; no application code was.
2. **Trace first.** Before fixing a failure: find it in neatlogs, write the hypothesis, fix, run again, compare. Each fix is a hardening record `HR-NNN` (Trigger, Diagnosis, Change, Before, After, Regression fixture).
3. **One commit per intent**, so one Entire checkpoint maps to one change.
4. **Evidence as we go.** Every named run appends a row to `evidence/ledger.jsonl` (UTC and IST time, git sha, fixture, arm, prompt version, neatlogs trace id, outcome, verdicts, repairs, tokens, cost, latency); traces are exported into `evidence/traces/`; `EVIDENCE.md` is generated, never hand-edited.
5. **Say what did not work.** Negative results stay in the record (HR-005 was tried and reverted; HR-002's first-page claim did not hold).
6. **Experiments have controls.** The ungated arm (B0) is the control for prompt changes; same-jobs A/B runs separate effects that were confounded.

## 3. Timeline (IST; shas are in `git log`)

### Friday 9 to Saturday 10 Oct, before 12:30: planning only
Accounts, access checks (Vertex Gemini, K2, AWS limits, neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai, Crustdata), the planning documents in `docs/planning/`, the repository with setup files. A launch motion-graphic was built outside the repository from the sister's drawings and brand assets (its sources were copied in later; the real drawings stay in the gitignored `_private/`).

### Saturday 12:30 to 14:30: the agent exists (M1 to M5)
- **12:30** first commit; **12:37** Entire Brain enabled; **12:48** ground-up design document ([DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md)).
- **12:52 to 13:00 (M1):** package scaffold, model clients (Gemini, K2), tracing wrapper, ledger; spikes against the real services, four traces read back through the neatlogs MCP.
- **13:04 (M2):** the oath engine: verdict object, promise catalogue, deterministic verifiers, a quote-checked K2 judge.
- **13:18 to 13:20 (M3):** LangGraph pipeline (safety screen, character card, oath, planner, page loop with repair, B0 arm, receipt) and the FastAPI app with server-sent events.
- **13:19 to 13:34:** safety eval over 26 fixture drawings (25/26 matched; the one unsafe drawing refused; no benign drawing refused); judge eval with injected faults (24/24 caught, 0/8 clean pages flagged, 0/88 judge calls unverifiable). **13:27** two neatlogs detections created.
- **13:40:** first real recovery run: image quota errors on four pictures, story shipped as text on those pages, receipt said so.
- **13:40 to 13:42:** the first two hardening changes (HR-001 prompt, HR-002 pipelined review), the EVIDENCE.md generator and linter.
- **14:12 (M5):** web app (React, Vite, Rive owl, demo mode). **14:18:** B2 arm (the same model reviews its own story) and the baseline sweep report. **14:32:** handoff note.
- Honest gap: this work was done in a session started outside the repository, so it has no Entire checkpoint.

### Saturday 14:30 to 17:00: measurement and the first records
- **Sweep 2** (prompt p2, arms B0, B1, B2, 84 jobs, 0 errors): shipped with a broken promise B0 27/28, **B1 0/28**, B2 27/28. The model reviewing itself did not close the gap.
- **15:08** first Entire checkpoints (the session now runs inside the repo). **15:21 to 15:24** HR-001 and HR-002 written; the HR-002 ablation (same 14 jobs, review sequential or pipelined) showed -35% total time but no gain in time to first page.
- Research (Remotion, HyperFrames, OpenEdit, agent-video-studio, Anthropic's harness posts) in [planning/video-harness.md](planning/video-harness.md).

### Saturday 17:00 to 20:00: the video agent, the model, the triage loop
- **17:20** HyperFrames spike: two renders byte-identical; the `check` gate caught a missing asset, overflow, low contrast and a script error.
- **17:41** the video agent: spec of typed blocks, numbers only as claim references resolved from evidence files, a video oath (length, claims sourced, claims match the ledger, no overclaiming words, tools covered, no secrets, no child data, renders clean, loudness), repair of the failing scene, a receipt. First run: 5 failures found by running it (see 5).
- **17:3x to 17:45** the cfo.ai model built through the MCP (by a delegated agent from the design in [planning/cfo.md](planning/cfo.md)); **18:00** neatlogs's own triage cards reviewed ([TRIAGE-REVIEW.md](../evidence/neatlogs/TRIAGE-REVIEW.md)).
- **17:46 to 18:28** HR-003 (sentence target), HR-004 (mild words), HR-005 (timeout: reverted); judge eval with the hackathon gateway models.
- **18:30 to 19:15** the first illustrated story from a fixture drawing (8 pictures, 8 narration clips) and its read-along video (3:37, all video promises passed); HR-006 (words painted into a picture).

### Saturday 19:15 to 21:00: closing the product gaps
- **19:42** grown-up promises (data, never instructions, judged per page), `DELETE /api/stories/{id}`, video endpoints; the web app gains a promise field, a "Make my movie" button and a Forget that deletes on the server.
- **20:00** quiz (four questions, each with a verbatim evidence line, five promises) and the picture-order game; healthy-play rules written into [WEB.md](WEB.md).
- **20:07** the neatlogs-measured cost replaced the estimate in cfo.ai (change 275839). **20:29** a full run through the real browser UI: drawing, lesson, promise, 8 pages, movie (3:45), Forget (the story 404s afterwards). It found the quiz-timing bug, fixed at **20:32**.

### Sunday 11 Oct, morning: documentation and the remaining items
Quiz-quality sweep (sweep 7), Entire Trails (runners scaffolded; blocked by the web step), the illustration policy (`pictures: full | half | none`) that came out of the cfo.ai model, anonymous check of the cfo.ai share link, and this documentation.

## 4. What the evidence says (so far)
| Claim | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Gating removes broken promises that a plain writer and a self-reviewing writer ship | `sweep-2-p2`: 27/28, 27/28, **0/28** ([report](../evidence/reports/20261010-1505-IST-sweep-2-p2.md)) |
| Each fix improved the agent, with numbers | [HR-001](../evidence/hardening/HR-001.md) to [HR-006](../evidence/hardening/HR-006.md) |
| The judge catches injected faults | `evidence/runs/20261010-1334-IST-judge-eval.json` (24/24, 0/88 unverifiable) |
| The agent recovers from a failed action | trace `94db23729dac6323368749acba4be1cb` |
| The product works through the real UI | the 20:29 run (`web/scripts/e2e-real.mjs`, screenshots in `evidence/screens/`) |
| Cost | neatlogs-measured text cost $0.0199 per gated story; pictures and voice are list-price assumptions ([TOOLS.md](TOOLS.md)) |

Tests that ran: 79 backend (`pytest tests`), 19 web (`npm run test` in `web/`), `ruff check` clean, the evidence linter (`python scripts/lint_evidence.py`).

## 5. What went wrong, in order (kept because it is the useful part)
1. **The B1 gate shipped broken promises in sweep 1** because three runs errored from bugs now fixed (unparseable page JSON, a missing image prompt).
2. **HR-001 looked like a pure prompt fix but B1 still overshot**; HR-003 followed. The control arm separated the effects.
3. **HR-002's headline was confounded** (the prompt fix also cut repairs), so a same-jobs ablation was run; it showed time to first page did not improve.
4. **HR-005 did not hold up**: a shorter timeout looked right from two traces and was worse in an A/B (the provider was slow at that time, so the result is inconclusive; we reverted).
5. **The video agent's first runs failed five ways**: the planner wrote the word "five" for a number field (we had told it to write no digits), the CLI wrote the file to a mangled path, narration was too slow (5:16 instead of about 1:00), the planner wrote "cryptographic receipts" (a new `no_overclaims` promise), and the brand fonts had no `@font-face` (the repair step could not fix it, so the loop now stops when a failure is not tied to a scene).
6. **Every page showed the same picture** in the first story videos: all pictures are named `image.jpg` and overwrote each other. Found only by looking at frames.
7. **The image model painted words into a picture** despite "no text in the image" (HR-006).
8. **The quiz never reached the child** in the first full browser run: it is verified after the story, and the child reached the last page first. The end screen now offers the quiz when it is ready.
9. **Keys pasted into the chat** twice; both ended up in session transcripts and in Entire checkpoints. Rotate both before publishing.
10. **Entire Trails and review cannot run** until the GitHub App is connected on entire.io (web step).

## 5b. What each part of the repository is
| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `src/storybound/` | the product: `pipeline.py` (graph), `agents/` (writer, planner, quizmaker, ...), `oath/` (catalogue, deterministic checks, engine, judge), `video/` (the video agent), `api.py`, `clients/` (Gemini, K2, images, TTS) |
| `web/` | the React app and its browser checks (`scripts/e2e-real.mjs`, `e2e-quiz-mock.mjs`) |
| `scripts/` | run and evidence tools: `sweep.py`, `report.py`, `run_story.py`, `story_video.py`, `make_video.py`, `quiz_story.py`, `build_evidence.py`, `lint_evidence.py`, `neatlogs_mcp.py` |
| `evidence/` | ledger, reports, hardening records, exported traces, screenshots, story packages, Entire and cfo.ai outputs |
| `docs/` | design, API, web, platforms, this process, the tool usage, the status; `planning/` holds the pre-kickoff plans |
| `video/harness/` | HyperFrames project template, vendored GSAP, claim catalogues |

## 6. Where to read next
[TOOLS.md](TOOLS.md) (how neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai were used), [STATUS.md](STATUS.md) (what is left), [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md), [API.md](API.md), [WEB.md](WEB.md), `hackathon.md`, `EVIDENCE.md`.

# Storybound

**A story agent that keeps its promises, and can prove it.** A child's drawing and a lesson go in. The agent writes an **oath** (a list of promises), checks every page against it **before the child sees it**, rewrites any page that breaks a promise, and ships a **receipt** for the grown-ups. Then: pictures and narration, a **quiz** whose every question is verified against the story, a picture-order game, a read-along **video** made from the finished story, and grown-up-written promises. Built for neatHack (10 to 12 Oct 2026) with neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai.

> Why it is not just a chat model with a good prompt: in our 84-run experiment the same writer shipped at least one broken promise in **27 of 28 stories** when ungated and in **27 of 28** when it reviewed its own story, and in **0 of 28** when an independent gate checked every page ([report](evidence/reports/20261010-1505-IST-sweep-2-p2.md)). Most broken promises were quality failures (answer position, lesson missing, reading level), not safety failures.

## Read this first
| If you want | Open |
| --- | --- |
| How it was built, hour by hour, and what went wrong | [docs/PROCESS.md](docs/PROCESS.md) |
| How neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai were used (architecture, implementation, runtime, reasoning, result) | [docs/TOOLS.md](docs/TOOLS.md) |
| What is done and what is left | [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) |
| Every claim with its evidence | [EVIDENCE.md](EVIDENCE.md) (generated) and `evidence/` |
| The agent's design | [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) |
| The HTTP contract | [docs/API.md](docs/API.md) |
| The web app, healthy-play rules | [docs/WEB.md](docs/WEB.md) |
| The build log, dated | [hackathon.md](hackathon.md) |
| State of every platform | [docs/PLATFORMS.md](docs/PLATFORMS.md) |

## The pieces
- **Story agent** (`src/storybound/`): safety screen, character card, oath, planner, page loop with pipelined review and repair (LangGraph), whole-story gate, quiz, pictures, narration, receipt. Arms: **B0** ungated, **B1** gated (the product), **B2** the same model reviews its own story.
- **Oath** (`src/storybound/oath/`): 22 core promises plus lesson-specific ones, grown-up promises and 6 quiz promises, checked by deterministic code and an independent judge (K2, a different model family from the writer) with a verbatim-quote check.
- **Video agent** (`src/storybound/video/`): plans or reads a spec of typed blocks, resolves every number from an evidence file, narrates, builds and renders with HyperFrames, checks its own **video oath**, repairs the failing scene, and ships a receipt. Used for the read-along video of a story and for the demo video.
- **Web app** (`web/`): draw, pick a lesson, read, quiz and game, movie, grown-ups area (receipt, settings, forget).
- **Evidence** (`evidence/`): the run ledger, sweep reports, six hardening records, exported neatlogs traces, screenshots, Entire and cfo.ai outputs.

## Numbers you can check
| What | Value | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stories shipped with a broken promise (B0 / B2 / B1) | 27/28, 27/28, **0/28** | `evidence/reports/*sweep-2-p2.md` |
| Hardening records, each with before and after | HR-001 to HR-006 | `evidence/hardening/` |
| Judge on 24 injected faults | 24/24 caught, 0/8 clean pages flagged | `evidence/runs/20261010-1334-IST-judge-eval.json` |
| Text cost per gated story, measured by neatlogs | $0.0199 | `evidence/neatlogs/20261010-2010-IST-measured-vs-estimated-cost.json` |
| Month-6 gross margin (cfo.ai, Main / Growth / Downside) | 67.2% / 55.2% / 40.9% (estimates) | https://app.cfo.ai/s/vGE_ZEwfQtpoxPrg |
| Tests | 79 backend, 19 web | `pytest tests`, `npm run test` in `web/` |

## Run it (development)
```powershell
uv sync                              # creates .venv from pyproject.toml
copy .env.example .env               # fill in the keys; never commit .env
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m uvicorn storybound.api:app --app-dir src --port 8000   # serves the API and web/dist
cd web; npm install; npm run build   # the web app, served at http://127.0.0.1:8000
```
Google credentials come from `gcloud auth application-default login`. Demo mode (no models, free): open `http://127.0.0.1:8000/?mock=1`.

Useful commands:
```powershell
.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\run_story.py benign/bunny-bow-carrot --lesson sharing --media --name my-run   # one story, one ledger row
.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\sweep.py --name my-sweep --arms B0,B1,B2 --fixtures ... --lessons sharing,honesty --k 2
.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\report.py --name my-sweep           # the sweep report
.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\story_video.py evidence\stories\bunny-sharing-2   # read-along video from a story package
.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\build_evidence.py; .venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\lint_evidence.py
node web\scripts\e2e-real.mjs        # a real story through the real UI (costs about $0.40 plus $0.04)
```

## Rules this project keeps (`CLAUDE.md`)
All code written inside the hackathon window (first commit Sat 10 Oct 12:30 IST); secrets only in `.env`; no real child's data in the repo, traces, ledger or posts (fixtures only; real drawings stay in the gitignored `_private/`); no Google ADK; AWS limits respected; no raw Crustdata data in the repo.

## Privacy and healthy play, in short
No accounts, ads, tracking or purchases. No timers, lives, streaks, scores or autoplay for the child; every game is skippable; practice results stay in the browser tab. A parent can **forget a story**: the server deletes its pictures, narration, drawing and video (`DELETE /api/stories/{id}`). neatlogs traces keep names and places redacted and expire on their own.

Do not make the repo public before deciding what to do about those checkpoint refs (Entire documents no removal of a pushed checkpoint).

# Status: what is done, what is left, who must act

Updated Sun 11 Oct 2026 (IST). Submission window: Mon 12 Oct 19:00 to 23:55 IST (confirmed by the builder). Evidence for every line is in `EVIDENCE.md`, `evidence/` and the documents linked.

## 1. Done

| Area | State | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Story agent (oath, pipelined review, repair, receipt; arms B0, B1, B2) | Done, 80 tests | [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md), `sweep-2-p2` |
| Safety screen over 26 fixture drawings | 25/26 matched, the unsafe one refused, no benign refused | `evidence/runs/*safety-eval*` |
| Judge on injected faults | 24/24 caught, 0/8 clean flagged, 0/88 unverifiable | `evidence/runs/20261010-1334-IST-judge-eval.json` |
| Experiments and hardening | Seven sweeps; HR-001 to HR-006 written; HR-007 below | `evidence/hardening/`, `evidence/reports/` |
| Recovery run | Image quota errors, story shipped as text on those pages, receipt said so | trace `94db23729dac6323368749acba4be1cb` |
| Pictures, narration, receipt | Real runs, two illustrated stories | `evidence/stories/` |
| Illustration policy | `pictures: full / half / none` (from the cfo.ai model) | API doc, `tests/test_pipeline.py` |
| Verified quiz | Four questions per story, six promises, judge on every question, dropped if unverified | `docs/WEB.md`, sweep 7 below |
| Picture-order game, healthy-play rules | Done; skippable, no timers, streaks, scores or autoplay | `docs/WEB.md`, `web/scripts/e2e-quiz-mock.mjs` |
| Grown-up promises | Done, end to end (appears on the receipt) | API doc, `tests/test_oath.py`, browser run |
| Forget a story (`DELETE /api/stories/{id}`) | Done; the story 404s afterwards | `tests/test_api.py`, browser run |
| Read-along video from a story | Done: 3:37 and 3:45 renders, all promises pass | `evidence/stories/bunny-sharing-2/video/receipt.json` |
| Web app through a real browser | Drawing, 8 pages, movie and Forget verified live | `web/scripts/e2e-real.mjs`, `evidence/screens/` |
| neatlogs | Traces, 7 detections, triage review, CLI signed in, measured cost | [TOOLS.md](TOOLS.md) |
| Entire | 37+ checkpoints, graph diffs, Brain, runners tailored | [TOOLS.md](TOOLS.md) |
| cfo.ai | Model built; measured cost in (change 275839); share link checked anonymously | [TOOLS.md](TOOLS.md), `evidence/cfo/` |
| Crustdata | Used once, derived counts only | `evidence/cfo/20261011-0850-IST-market-note-crustdata.md` |
| Documentation | PROCESS, TOOLS, STATUS, PLATFORMS, DESIGN addendum, API, WEB, README, HANDOFF | this folder |

### Quiz quality (sweep `sweep-7-quiz`, gated arm, 7 drawings x 2 lessons x 2 seeds)
<<QUIZ>>

### HR-007: quota errors (found by sweep 7)
<<HR7>>

## 2. Left, and who must act

### Only the builder can do these
| # | Item | Why it is blocked | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Rotate the neatlogs key and the hackathon gateway key** | Both were pasted into the session and are in Entire checkpoint transcripts (some already on the private `origin`) | Rotate; update `.env`; then decide what to do about the pushed checkpoint refs before any public push |
| 2 | **Entire Trails and review** | `entire trail create` and `entire review` answer "repository not found": the Entire GitHub App is not installed on `hatif03/storybound` | On entire.io: Configure GitHub App, choose the repo, enable Trails. Then run `entire trail create --title "..." --type feature`, `entire review general`, `entire trail watch`; save outputs under `evidence/entire/` |
| 3 | **Checkpoint link for judges** | The repo is private; the link needs access | Either add the judges as collaborators or publish the repo (after item 1), then open `https://entire.io/gh/hatif03/storybound/commit/<FULL_SHA>` in a private window and record the sha and the 26-character checkpoint id |
| 4 | **neatlogs write-access steps** | The CLI login has read-only scopes (alert rules need `configuration:write`) | Approve a second sign-in with write scopes (link offered in the chat), or create in the dashboard: a human evaluation of 20 judge verdicts, alerts on cost and latency per story, a guest link for one trace |
| 5 | **cfo.ai UI steps** | Not available through the MCP | Screenshot Version history (change 275839), download the workbook, keep both in `evidence/cfo/` |
| 6 | **`#neatHack` posts and the submission post** | Posting is the builder's act | Log each in `evidence/posts.md` (URL, time, what it shows); content ideas in `docs/planning/content.md` |
| 7 | **Demo video (last)** | Requested last | `scripts/make_video.py` with `requires_coverage` (see HANDOFF.md); at most 3:00 |
| 8 | **Publish decision** | See items 1 and 3 | After rotation: `build_evidence.py`, `lint_evidence.py`, publish, quote-post Mon 12 Oct 19:00 to 23:55 IST |

### Work that can still be done (not blocking)
| Item | Note |
| --- | --- |
| Price the quiz and video add-ons in cfo.ai | Cost per quiz is measured in sweep 7 (see above); the model has no add-on row yet |
| One live run with `pictures=half` through the browser | The policy is unit-tested; a live run through `e2e-real.mjs --pictures half` would show an unpainted page in the reader |
| Judge-reviewed quiz questions from more stories and ages | All runs were age 6; the quiz was reviewed by hand on one story and measured by the promises on 28 |
| Safari, touch devices, screen reader | Not verified (see `docs/WEB.md`); the browser checks use desktop Edge |
| Ages other than 6; languages other than English | Not tested |

## 3. Known limits (said plainly)
- Costs of pictures and narration are list-price assumptions; neatlogs prices text only. The true figure is on the Google Cloud bill, which we have not read.
- The evidence videos are made from fixture drawings only; the sister's real drawings were never put through the pipeline for the repository.
- Early work (before 15:08 on 10 Oct) has no Entire checkpoint; `entire why` shows older code as human-written.
- The picture-order game and quiz were checked in demo mode and in sweeps; a live verified quiz played through the browser UI is covered by the last browser run (see HANDOFF.md for the latest result).
- neatlogs retention on the free plan is 14 days; traces are exported to the repo.
- The judge (K2) is a different model family from the writer, but not a human; human agreement was not measured (item 4).

## 4. Risks
| Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- |
| Pasted keys in checkpoints | Rotate; do not publish until decided |
| A model quota error ending a run | HR-007 backoff; the receipt states degradations |
| Render time for the movie (about 7 minutes for 3:45) | The API runs it in the background with a status endpoint; one render at a time |
| Judges cannot open the Entire link | Item 3 |

# HR-007: a per-minute quota error ended a run (quota errors back off longer)

Date: 11 Oct 2026. Found by `sweep-7-quiz`, not by a check.

## Trigger

Two of the first 28 jobs in `sweep-7-quiz` (both `christmas-tree-digital`, seed 1, lessons sharing and honesty) ended with `outcome: error` at the **first model call** (28 and 33 seconds in): `ClientError: 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` from Vertex. Traces `65e993be95cd003911afdba708ec4f5f` and `7a6682c07ff2835882e798d06a43a396`. A child would have seen the generic "something went wrong" message. At that moment a real-UI browser run was making a story at the same time as the 5-worker sweep, so the quota was under unusual load.

## Diagnosis

Hypothesis: the retry helper tries a retryable error 3 times with waits of about 1 s and 2 s. A per-minute quota needs seconds to clear, so three quick tries all hit the same wall. Images already used a 6 s base for this reason (commit `fbb832b`); text calls did not.

## Change

- Commit `4890215` (Entire checkpoint `01M4MF7NVG93PCH5FXTQJJEXG8`): `with_retry` waits four times longer on a 429 and allows one more attempt (waits of 4, 8 and 16 s over four tries). Other errors are unchanged.
- Regression test `test_retry_waits_longer_and_tries_once_more_on_a_quota_error` (four tries with waits of at least 4 s on a 429; three tries and short waits on a 503).

## Before and after

| | Before (old retry) | After (new retry) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The two failed jobs | error at 28 s and 33 s | re-run under the new code: both **shipped** (86 s and 97 s, 1 repair each) |
| Jobs that ended on a 429 across all earlier sweeps | 0 of about 330 (the quota was never this loaded before) | 0 |

Read this honestly: two jobs is a tiny sample, the load that caused the first failures was not repeated on the re-run, and the quota may simply have been quieter. The test pins the behaviour; the re-run shows the stories complete. It does not prove the new backoff would have survived the same burst.

## Regression fixture

`tests/test_basics.py::test_retry_waits_longer_and_tries_once_more_on_a_quota_error`. Re-run job: `benign/christmas-tree-digital`, lessons sharing and honesty, seed 1, arm B1.
E

input.prompt: How can secrets be redacted from checkpoint transcripts: is there a way to add custom redaction patterns or regexes (settings keys), how does the built-in secret scanner (Betterleaks) work, can redaction be applied retroactively to existing checkpoints, and is there a setting to not push session transcripts? result.output:
**Redacting secrets from checkpoints**

Entire redacts API keys, access tokens, credentialed URLs, database connection strings, and private keys before it writes checkpoint metadata. Secret scanning is on by default.

**Custom redaction patterns**

- `redaction.custom_redactions`: a label-to-regex map that produces the bare `REDACTED` token. Example: `"acme_token": "ACME_TOKEN_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}"`.
- `redaction.pii.custom_patterns`: a label-to-regex map where each label becomes `[REDACTED_<LABEL>]`. Example: `"employee_id": "EMP-\\d{6}"` produces `[REDACTED_EMPLOYEE_ID]`.
- Rule packs: YAML or JSON files in `.entire/redactors/` (shared) or `.entire/redactors/local/` (personal). Patterns use Go RE2 syntax, so lookarounds and backreferences are unavailable.

Put shared rules in `.entire/settings.json` and private rules in `.entire/settings.local.json`. Entries merge per key.

**How Betterleaks works**

Betterleaks is the default secret scanner, controlled by `redaction.betterleaks.enabled` (default `true`, project settings only). It covers "several hundred known secret formats." The page does not describe its matching internals. goredact, controlled by `redaction.goredact.enabled` (default `false`), checks a smaller set of token shapes with structural validators such as length or checksums. At least one scanner must stay enabled. CLI 0.10.2 uses Betterleaks without scanner selection. The scanner keys first appear in `v0.10.3-nightly.202608210613.680d64782`.

**Retroactive redaction**

The page doesn't say whether redaction can be applied to existing checkpoints. It states only that rule changes "take effect on the next CLI or hook invocation."

**Not pushing session transcripts**

The page doesn't document a setting or CLI flag that stops transcripts from being pushed. The closest options only affect the OpenAI Privacy Filter pass, not whether content is pushed:
- `redaction.openai_privacy_filter.prompt_default` set to `"never"` skips that pass.
- `ENTIRE_OPF=no git push` skips it for one push.

**CLI flags**

The page documents no CLI flags for redaction. It lists these environment variables: `ENTIRE_OPF`, `ENTIRE_OPF_BOOTSTRAP_LIMIT`, `ENTIRE_OPF_BATCH_LIMIT`, `ENTIRE_EXTERNALIZE_IMAGES`, and `ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT`. To verify settings, run `entire status --detailed`.

# History rewrite, Sun 11 Oct 2026 (IST)

**Why.** Two things in the git history should not have been public: (1) the hackathon gateway key, which was pasted into the session and was therefore stored in three files of Entire checkpoint transcripts (`full.jsonl`, `prompt.txt`, `transcript.jsonl`); (2) six images in `video/launch/img/`: four drawings by the builder's sister and two cutouts of her (face covered by a cartoon). The builder approved the rewrite and gave consent for her drawings, and asked that the images stay out of the repository.

**What was done** (tool: `git filter-repo`, run on a full local backup):
- The six image files were removed from every commit; `video/launch/img/` and `_private/` are now in `.gitignore`. The images stay on the builder's disk so the launch video still renders locally.
- The exact text of each key held in `.env` (neatlogs, Crustdata, K2, gateway) was replaced by `***REMOVED-<NAME>***` in every file of every commit on every ref, including `refs/entire/checkpoints/*`. Only the gateway key was actually present; the neatlogs key had already been masked by Entire as `REDACTED`. The rule file was kept outside the repository and holds no key text in any commit.
- `.entire/settings.json` now carries `redaction.custom_redactions` for the three key shapes, so new checkpoints mask them too.

**Check afterwards** (counts only, nothing printed): 153 commits scanned on all refs; 0 files contain any of the four key values; 0 commits touch any of the six image paths; `entire checkpoint list` and `entire checkpoint explain <id>` still resolve (checkpoint ids are not git shas, so they are unchanged).

**What changed for readers.** All commit shas changed from the first commit that touched a removed file onward (84 of 153). `sha-map.txt` (old, new) is in this folder. Short shas quoted in `EVIDENCE.md`, `docs/TOOLS.md`, `hackathon.md`, `evidence/hardening/*`, `evidence/ledger.jsonl` and three graph-diff file names were re-pointed to the new shas with the same map; dates, authors and messages are unchanged. Nothing was backdated and no work was hidden: the content of every kept file is the same except for the removed images and the replaced key text.

**Limits, said plainly.**
- GitHub keeps unreachable objects for a while and cached views may exist, and the old history was already on the private origin before the rewrite. The gateway key and neatlogs key must still be rotated; the builder said they will.
- The pasted keys also live in the local, gitignored `.entire/metadata/` of this machine and in the Claude session transcript outside the repository.
